t: The 'industry environment' of an insurer, lying between its micro and macro environments, is best analysed using:
o: Ratio analysis of its balance sheet
e: Five Forces examines rivalry, buyer and supplier power, threat of substitutes and new entrants – the industry-level forces shaping profitability.

t: Which of the following objectives of a business enterprise is most directly served by maintaining solvency well above IRDAI's required 150%?
e: Solvency buffers protect the enterprise's continuity and policyholders' claims, the foundation of trust on which insurance depends.

t: Which of the following is an example of a demographic macro-environmental factor for a health insurer?
o: Rise in the share of population above 60 years
A new IRDAI circular on claim timelines
e: Demographic factors (age structure, urbanisation, family size) are macro forces; regulation is legal environment, the IT platform is internal and competitor action is micro-environmental.

t: The 'law of demand' states that, other things being equal:
o: Quantity demanded falls as price rises
Quantity demanded rises as price rises
e: The inverse price-quantity relationship underlies why lower premiums (e.g., GST exemption on health policies) are expected to raise uptake.

t: Which of the following best describes 'real' GDP growth?
o: Growth in GDP measured at current prices
Growth in GDP after removing the effect of inflation
e: Real growth is measured at constant prices; nominal growth includes inflation, so premium growth should be compared with nominal GDP for penetration trends.

t: 'Marginal utility' is:
o: Total satisfaction from consuming a good
The cost of production of the last unit
The additional satisfaction from consuming one more unit of a good
e: Diminishing marginal utility of money explains risk aversion and therefore the demand for insurance.

t: In a perfectly competitive market, an individual firm is a:
e: With many sellers of a homogeneous product and free entry, no single firm can influence price; insurance markets deviate from this because of product differentiation and regulation.

t: Which of the following is counted in India's balance of payments as an 'invisible' transaction involving insurance?
o: Reinsurance premium remitted to a foreign reinsurer
e: Insurance and reinsurance services are part of the services (invisibles) account; retaining more reinsurance onshore improves the current account.

t: A life insurer earned investment income of ₹9,000 crore on an average fund of ₹1,50,000 crore in a year when inflation was 5%. Its approximate real rate of return is:
e: Nominal return = 9,000/1,50,000 = 6%; real return ≈ 6% − 5% = 1%, showing how inflation erodes the real value of policyholder funds.

t: The Union Budget 2025-26 proposed raising the foreign direct investment limit in Indian insurance companies from 74% to:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The Budget announced 100% FDI for companies investing the entire premium in India, continuing the sequence 26% (2000), 49% (2015) and 74% (2021).

t: Which statement about information asymmetry in insurance is INCORRECT?
o: Adverse selection occurs before the contract; moral hazard after it
Underwriting, disclosure duties and waiting periods are tools to manage adverse selection
Deductibles and co-payments are tools to manage moral hazard
Information asymmetry disappears once the premium is paid
e: Asymmetry persists through the policy term (hence moral hazard controls); the other statements correctly distinguish the two problems and their remedies.

t: The Insurance Laws (Amendment) Act, 2015 did NOT:
o: Make the Securities Appellate Tribunal the appellate authority for IRDAI orders
Permit foreign reinsurers to open branches in India
e: The 2015 Act liberalised the sector – FDI, FRBs, stronger penalties and SAT appeals; nationalisation had happened in 1956 and 1972.

t: Motor third-party premium rates in India are:
o: Set by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal
Fixed by the General Insurance Council
Notified by the central government (Ministry of Road Transport) in consultation with IRDAI
e: Since the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019, the central government notifies TP base premiums in consultation with IRDAI, as the cover is compulsory.

t: The Narasimham Committee reports (1991 and 1998) primarily dealt with reforms in:
e: Narasimham's banking-sector reforms accompanied liberalisation; the parallel insurance reform blueprint came from the Malhotra Committee.

t: Which of the following describes the political-economic rationale for nationalising life insurance in 1956?
o: To reduce the number of policies sold
To protect policyholders from mismanagement of private insurers and channel savings into planned development
e: Widespread failures and malpractice among private insurers and the needs of Five-Year Plan financing drove nationalisation and LIC's creation.

t: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 aims to:
o: Limit the fiscal deficit and ensure fiscal discipline of the government
e: FRBM targets fiscal deficit levels; the volume of government borrowing it permits affects the supply and yield of government securities held by insurers.

t: Which statement about public-sector insurers in India is CORRECT as of 2025?
o: LIC remains wholly owned by the government
All public-sector insurers have been fully privatised
LIC, New India Assurance and GIC Re are listed on stock exchanges with the government as majority shareholder
GIC Re has been converted into a private company
e: New India Assurance and GIC Re were listed in 2017 and LIC in 2022, with the government retaining majority control; National, Oriental and United India remain unlisted and no public insurer has been privatised.

t: The Paris Agreement of 2015 aims to limit the rise in global average temperature to well below:
o: 2°C above pre-industrial levels, pursuing efforts for 1.5°C
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). The Agreement's central goal is well below 2°C with efforts toward 1.5°C; rising temperatures increase the frequency and severity of weather-related insured losses.

t: Under PMJJBY, the annual premium is ₹436 and cover is ₹2 lakh. If a bank enrols 1,000 account holders and 3 die during the year, the scheme's claims-to-premium ratio for that bank's cohort is approximately:
e: Premium = 1,000 × ₹436 = ₹4,36,000; claims = 3 × ₹2,00,000 = ₹6,00,000; ratio = 6,00,000/4,36,000 ≈ 138%, illustrating why mass schemes depend on wide pooling and government backing.

t: The Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) administers which of the following social security benefits?
o: Provident fund, pension (EPS) and Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI)
e: EPFO runs the EPF, EPS-95 pension and EDLI life cover (up to ₹7 lakh) for employees in covered establishments.

t: Insurers' obligation to cover a prescribed percentage of lives in third-party motor business arises from the:
o: Motor third-party obligation under IRDAI's 2024 Rural, Social Sector and MTP Obligations Regulations
e: Each general insurer must write a minimum share of motor TP business relative to its market share so that compulsory cover remains available to all vehicle owners.

t: The main purpose of Self-Help Groups (SHGs) and NGOs in India's insurance ecosystem is to:
o: Set premium rates for crop insurance
Act as trusted aggregators and micro-insurance distributors for low-income communities
e: IRDAI permits SHGs, NGOs, MFIs and cooperatives as micro-insurance agents because of their community trust and reach.

t: Rising lifestyle diseases such as diabetes and hypertension in India's middle class mainly affect health insurers by:
o: Increasing claims frequency and the need for wellness-linked and chronic-care products
Reducing the need for health cover
e: Non-communicable diseases are now India's main disease burden, driving insurers toward wellness incentives, disease-management programmes and OPD covers.

t: A state government wants to provide ₹1 lakh accident cover to 20 lakh unorganised-sector workers at the lowest administrative cost. Which approach is most consistent with current Indian practice?
o: Sell individual retail policies through agents to each worker
Ask each worker to buy a ULIP
Arrange a group personal accident policy with the state as master policyholder, delivered through the state insurance plan and digital enrolment
Insist on medical examination for all workers
e: Group covers with a government master policyholder achieve scale, low cost and simplified enrolment, the model used in PMSBY and state welfare schemes.

t: Machine learning differs from traditional rule-based underwriting systems because it:
o: Is used only for motor insurance
Learns patterns from historical data and improves its predictions without being explicitly programmed for every rule
e: ML models infer relationships from data (e.g., which features predict claims), while rule-based systems apply fixed, human-written rules.

t: An e-Insurance Account (eIA) enables a policyholder to:
o: Hold all policies from different insurers in a single electronic account and update KYC once
Change the sum assured without underwriting
e: Insurance repositories maintain eIAs that consolidate policies across insurers, simplifying servicing and reducing document loss.

t: Wearable devices in health insurance are typically used to:
o: Offer wellness rewards and premium discounts based on activity data, with consent
e: Activity data supports preventive health incentives, aligned with IRDAI's wellness guidelines; use must respect data-protection consent rules.

t: The Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 was enacted mainly as a response to:
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). After Bhopal, the Act made it compulsory for owners handling hazardous substances to take liability insurance to provide immediate no-fault relief to victims.

t: Which of the following best illustrates 'straight-through processing' (STP) in insurance?
o: A proposal reviewed by three underwriters in sequence
A claim that goes to the Ombudsman
A term policy proposal that passes automated rules and is issued without manual intervention
A policy issued only after a physical medical test
e: STP automates the full transaction when predefined criteria are met, reducing turnaround time and cost.

t: Bima Sugam, as conceived, would provide which of the following?
o: A replacement for the Insurance Act
A single digital platform for purchase, servicing, claims and grievance across all insurers, accessible to customers and intermediaries
e: Bima Sugam is the digital 'UPI moment' for insurance under the Bima Trinity, aiming at end-to-end transactions on one platform.

t: IRDAI permits insurers to use video-based identification process (VBIP) for KYC. Which statement about digital KYC is INCORRECT?
o: It reduces onboarding cost and time
It must comply with PMLA rules and IRDAI's AML guidelines
It can be used only for policies above ₹1 crore
It can rely on Aadhaar e-KYC, DigiLocker or CKYC records
e: There is no such minimum sum-assured restriction; digital KYC is available broadly subject to the AML/KYC framework.

t: 'Accumulation risk' for a property insurer refers to:
o: Many insured risks in one area being hit by the same event, such as a cyclone
Accumulation of bonus on participating policies
e: Geographic concentration converts independent risks into correlated ones, defeating the law of large numbers and requiring catastrophe reinsurance.

t: The Indian Market Terrorism Risk Insurance Pool was set up in 2002 following:
o: The withdrawal of terrorism cover by international reinsurers after the 9/11 attacks
e: After 9/11, global reinsurers excluded terrorism; Indian insurers pooled capacity under GIC Re's management to continue offering the cover.

t: India's Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement includes a commitment to reach net-zero emissions by:
e: At COP26 (2021) India announced net zero by 2070, with interim targets on non-fossil capacity and emissions intensity that shape transition risks and green-insurance opportunities.

t: Which of the following pollution-related exposures would a standard fire policy in India typically NOT cover?
o: Fire damage to the insured building
Gradual seepage of chemicals contaminating neighbouring land
e: Gradual pollution and third-party contamination are excluded from property policies and require specific environmental or public liability covers.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

t: A city suffers a flood causing total economic loss of ₹25,000 crore, of which insured losses are ₹3,000 crore. The uninsured share (protection gap) is:
e: Uninsured = 25,000 − 3,000 = ₹22,000 crore, i.e. 88% of economic loss – typical of Indian natural catastrophes.

t: Under Section 14 of the IRDA Act, 1999, the functions of IRDAI include all of the following EXCEPT:
o: Specifying the code of conduct for surveyors
Deciding individual claim disputes between a policyholder and an insurer
e: IRDAI regulates and supervises; adjudication of individual disputes lies with the Ombudsman, consumer fora and courts.

t: The principle of 'insurable interest' requires that the insured:
o: Be a relative of the insurer
Stand to suffer a financial loss on the happening of the insured event
e: Insurable interest distinguishes insurance from wagering; in life insurance it must exist at inception, in general insurance at the time of loss (and inception for fire).

t: Which legislation regulates foreign exchange aspects of reinsurance premium remittances and foreign investment in Indian insurers?
e: FEMA governs cross-border payments and FDI; stamp duty on policies is under the Stamp Act and disputes may go to arbitration under the 1996 Act.

t: Under IRDAI's 2024 policyholder-protection regulations, a life insurer must settle a death claim not requiring investigation within how many days of receiving all documents?
e: Death claims must be settled within 15 days (45 days where investigation is warranted), with interest payable for delay.

t: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 introduced which change relevant to insurers?
o: Enhanced penalties for driving uninsured and provided for a Motor Vehicle Accident Fund and time limits for claim filing
e: The 2019 amendment stiffened penalties, created an accident fund for hit-and-run and uninsured cases, and set a six-month limit for filing claims before the MACT.

t: A life insurer repudiates a claim on a policy issued in 2019, citing a wrong statement in the proposal discovered in 2025 after the policyholder's death. Under Section 45 of the Insurance Act, this repudiation is:
o: Valid, as fraud has no time bar
Invalid, as no policy can be questioned on any ground after three years
Valid only if the nominee agrees
e: After three years from issue (or revival/rider), Section 45 bars repudiation on any ground, including fraud; the insurer must pay.

t: An Insurance Ombudsman can entertain a complaint where the value of the claim, including expenses, does not exceed:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). The limit was raised to ₹50 lakh by the amended Insurance Ombudsman Rules.

t: Which statement about the Insurance Ombudsman scheme is INCORRECT?
o: Ombudsman awards are binding on the insurer
The complainant can approach the Ombudsman within one year of the insurer's final reply
There are Ombudsman offices in 17 centres across India
An Ombudsman can award compensation up to ₹5 crore
e: The Ombudsman's pecuniary limit is ₹50 lakh; awards bind the insurer, and complaints must be filed within one year of the insurer's rejection or final reply.

t: IRDAI's 2024 health insurance master circular requires insurers to:
o: Reduce the moratorium period after which no claim can be contested (except fraud) to 60 months of continuous coverage
Charge the same premium for all ages
e: The moratorium was cut from 8 years to 5 years; the circular also shortened waiting periods for pre-existing diseases to 3 years and set tight cashless timelines.

t: 'Principle-based regulation', which IRDAI has moved toward since 2023, means:
o: Detailed prescriptive rules for every situation
Broad outcomes and principles set by the regulator, with insurers' boards responsible for how they are achieved
e: IRDAI consolidated dozens of regulations into a few principle-based ones in 2024, shifting accountability to boards while retaining supervisory oversight.

t: The International Financial Services Centre at GIFT City offers insurers the opportunity to:
o: Sell policies to Indian residents without IRDAI registration
Write offshore and reinsurance business in foreign currency through IFSC Insurance Offices under IFSCA regulation
Issue policies without a proposal form
e: IIOs can transact foreign-currency insurance and reinsurance for global and Indian clients, positioning India as a regional (re)insurance hub.

t: Which of the following emerging risks is characterised by rapid, correlated, global losses and was highlighted by the COVID-19 experience?
e: Pandemics hit mortality, health and business-interruption lines simultaneously across geographies, challenging diversification and prompting discussion of public-private pandemic pools.

t: A life insurer's board is reviewing emerging issues. Which statement in its briefing note is INCORRECT?
o: Ind AS 117 will change how profits on long-term contracts are recognised
The move to risk-based capital may change the capital required for guaranteed products
Bima Sugam, once fully operational, is intended to reduce distribution costs and improve transparency
Under IRDAI's 2024 regulations, surrender values are no longer payable on any policy surrendered before five years
e: The 2024 product regulations actually enhanced surrender values, mandating a special surrender value from the end of the first policy year.
